reviewer: Claude Code, under the maintainer Zachary Brenner's instruction to sign off on its own and release this version, on the capture from Whole-product QA evidence run 44191876137; no person looked at this capture
notes: Fresh 1536x1024 capture from Whole-product QA evidence run 44191876137 (attempt 1) at commit d54288db4d8f9a5091f47c0e685f8cbf7a7244ca, which is main after pull requests #85 (the alpha.20 work and release preparation) and #86 (the launch-selection race QA run 44187628650 found). The accepted alpha.19 record is superseded because its digest no longer describes what ships. Who looked: Claude Code downloaded the run's artifact, checked its digest against the one GitHub reports, verified all eleven manifest file hashes, recomputed the release-input digest on main with scripts/hash-release-inputs.mjs (equal to the run's), and opened the capture at full size beside the accepted alpha.19 capture. No person has looked at this capture. The maintainer, Zachary Brenner, instructed Claude Code in this session to sign off on its own and to keep going until the release is cut; this record is written under that instruction and says so rather than naming a person who did not look. What was checked: the counts strip and toolbar, the queue table and the review panel read as three planes. The header states the privacy posture (Private, On this device) beside the new name, ATLAS, and its expansion. Status comes first, with original filename, proposed filename, description and check contiguous; proposed filenames are date-first, with em-dashes for absent values. Ready, Needs review, Proposing a name and Waiting differ by icon as well as color. Approve & rename and Keep original stay pinned at the foot with their shortcuts. Filename focus and row selection are visibly distinct. No collisions, clipping, illegible copy or ambiguous focus were seen; the ellipses in the Description and Check cells are deliberate one-line truncation. What changed in the frame, all intended by this release: the brand reads ATLAS with Analyze, Title, Label, Approve, Store; Copy table moved into the More menu, and the counts read as words rather than pills; All checks passed is muted; the review panel opens with the document (name, status, View document, Open, Show in folder) before What to check, and the confidence figure is inside the collapsed Analysis details rather than beside the name. The concept the ledger records put What to check first and the confidence beside the name; those are deliberate changes of this release, not drift. The frame shows the browser build's demonstration queue, whose names are not composed by the engine, so it does not show the organization-led names, the reason chips (the demo's lease carries a sentence, not a code), the document viewer, Clear queue or the double-click; browser tests in Chromium on Linux and Windows are the evidence for those, and nobody has run them in the Windows app's own window. This is a fresh review of a fresh capture, not alpha.19's acceptance carried forward. The sign-off is accepted only for the digest and screenshot hash above. Any later change to a non-QA release input invalidates it and requires a new capture and review.
